title: Microrate Playback: interactive token-cost composer and pricing scenario scrubber
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design an interactive 'Microrate Playback' panel for the Redwood Console that lets users replay token-level billing across sessions and pricing slabs, compose pricing scenarios, and export timed slices. The feature supports forensic analysis, billing explanations for customers, and rapid hypothesis testing of pricing changes via an editable scenario scrubber and CSV/JSON export templates.
goals: Provide an intuitive scrubber to replay token consumption and per-token unit costs over time for a selected time range or session
Enable rapid scenario editing: swap pricing tiers, apply quantization profiles, and preview cost deltas in real time
Support export of composed scenarios and raw token events to CSV/JSON with time-aligned columns for downstream accounting
Surface attribution links to routes, model variants, and prompt families so teams can narrow root cause of cost spikes
acceptance_criteria: Proto: interactive Figma prototype demonstrates scrubber scrubbing across a 30-minute session and updates cost chart within 200ms
CSV/JSON export template includes columns: timestamp, user_id (anonymized), route, model_variant, token_count, token_cost_usd, cumulative_cost_usd
Attribution pane can filter by route/model/prompt and show top-5 contributors with percentage share
Design reviewed and approved by PM (James Chen) and Eng lead (Priya Nair) with a consolidated implementation doc linked
decisions: Use timeline scrubber (single-handle) rather than frame-by-frame playback to avoid perf issues with long sessions
Export format will default to CSV for accountancy teams and JSON for analytics pipelines; include a compact 'billing slice' flavor for quick downloads
Attribution ranking will be computed server-side and surfaced via a paginated list to avoid transferring full token logs to the client
tradeoffs: Client-side playback with full token event streaming gives the smoothest UI but increases client memory; chosen approach streams compact events and diffs to balance UX and memory
Showing per-token cost on hover is precise but noisy; instead we aggregate into 1s buckets with option to expand to raw events for exported slices
Realtime scenario recalculation may increase backend load; throttled updates (250ms debounce) recommended for initial rollout
design_notes: Primary layout: left column timeline scrubber + stacked area chart (cost by contributor), right column attribution stack and scenario editor
Microcopy: default export label 'Billing slice — anonymized' with toggles for PII columns
Interaction: scrubber drag updates chart and attribution; play button animates 1s buckets; shift+drag to select custom slice range
Pricing pattern controls: dropdown to apply pricing slab presets, switch to 'custom' to enter per-token USD or percent discount
Export UX: contextual export button with three options — Current view, Selected slice, Full session. Show estimated file size before download
